requirement_text.REQ-364:
Implements REQ-363's design artefact exactly — no new schema decisions here, this requirement is implementation of an already-validated design, matching this project's own CODE-DESIGNER-then-ELIXIR-DEV split for every other schema-bearing feature.

SCOPE: the `Letflow.Help` context module (naming follows this project's existing per-domain-context convention, e.g. `Letflow.Identity`, `Letflow.TenantProvisioning`) exposing: create a draft, update a draft, publish (draft -> live, sets confirmed_at), re-confirm (bumps confirmed_at on an already-live row without changing body — the explicit "I checked this, it's still accurate" action), and read (by screen_id + tenant prefix, or by process_definition_id). Every write path enforces REQ-363's sanitization rule from that design, not a weakened version of it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the tenant-facing authoring UI (REQ-365 for platform, a separate future requirement for the tenant admin UI itself — this requirement's acceptance criteria stop at a working, tested context module, callable from IEx/tests, not yet wired to any HTTP route or frontend component). Route/controller wiring, if this project's own API-surface convention wants a separate requirement for it (matching the pattern most REQ-027..030-style definition CRUD work already used), is a natural fast-follow, not bundled here — state explicitly in this requirement's close-out whether a route was added or deliberately deferred, rather than leaving it ambiguous.

result.summary:
RECONSTRUCTION NOTE: this handoff was originally written live during WF02-REQ364-20260917's security-review saga as ad-hoc, non-schema JSON (informal top-level keys such as req/at/result-as-bare-string instead of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's real schema), the exact anti-pattern this session's own ISS-0692 precedent names. It has been rewritten into full schema conformance by a later ORCH session under §4.1's not_agent_attested mechanism. created_at/started_at/completed_at are all set to the file's own git-introducing-commit timestamp (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A --format=%aI --reverse -- <path>`), the best-available real timestamp, NOT the original live dispatch/claim/completion times, which were never recorded in schema-legal fields on disk. All findings, quoted test counts, and verification detail below are migrated verbatim in substance from the original ad-hoc file; nothing was invented or paraphrased away.

3 of 4 ACs already sufficiently covered by the 54 existing tests. AC4 (confirmed_for_definition_version) had a real partial gap: original tests used a fixed process-definition version throughout, so reconfirm/2 merely replaying the stored value instead of re-reading fresh would have passed unnoticed. Added test:792-812 bumping the process definition's version between publish and reconfirm, asserting reconfirm reflects the NEW version. Verified via mutation testing: reverted resolve_confirmed_version to reuse the stale stored value, got 54/55 (only the new test failed), reverted mutant cleanly (git diff help.ex empty afterward).

VERIFICATION: mix letflow.check.test hit the documented stale-tenant_template-schema anti-pattern on first run (18 stale letflow_test* DBs predating help_content's migration) -- dropped them per docs/anti-patterns.md's documented fix, reran clean. help_test.exs: 55/55 consistently. Full suite runs 2-3: only pre-existing unrelated failures (a known ContextTest partition-race flake, REQ-369's already-known-unrelated impl_order gate failures).
result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to independently reproduce the mutation test and spot-check coverage against AC2/AC3.
